topic: 7 strange borders countdown ending on Nathu La, Sikkim
hook: Your Nathu La visit puts you a few steps from Chinese soldiers, and that is the last border on this list.
title: 7 Borders That Make No Sense, Ending in Sikkim
description:
A countdown of seven real borders that look fake on the map: a road through Canada to reach America, a Spanish town inside France, a German village on Swiss money, and more. The last stop is Nathu La in Sikkim, where Indian visitors can stand metres from Chinese soldiers.

#borders #geography #nathula
comment_prompt: Which border would you visit first?

scenes.narration: Your Nathu La visit puts you a few steps from Chinese soldiers, and that is the last border on this list.
scenes.headline: Metres From China

scenes.narration: Here are seven real borders, each one stranger than the one before. Every one of them is on the map today.
scenes.headline: 7 Real Borders

scenes.narration: One road leaves a country and comes back without turning. One village is German, but sits inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Roads And Villages

scenes.narration: One road was shut for aeroplanes. And one border is a ceremony that happens every evening.
scenes.headline: Shut For Planes

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see why the pass at Nathu La is the strangest of them all.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest

scenes.narration: Let us start the countdown, with a piece of America that you cannot reach by driving through America.
scenes.headline: Countdown Starts

scenes.narration: Number seven: Point Roberts, in Washington state. It is part of America, but you cannot drive there from America.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: The border follows the 49th parallel, a straight line on the map that ignores the shape of the land.
scenes.headline: A Straight Line

scenes.narration: That line cuts across a small peninsula, so the tip ended up American while everything around it stayed Canadian.
scenes.headline: Cut By A Line

scenes.narration: To reach Point Roberts by road, you drive into Canada first. Then you drive out again, back into the United States.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: Residents cross borders just to reach the rest of their own country. Shopping, doctors and work can all mean a queue.
scenes.headline: Passport To Go Home

scenes.narration: Boats and small planes can get there without touching Canada. But for most people, the road runs through another country.
scenes.headline: Boat Or Canada

scenes.narration: When the border closed to non-essential travel in 2020, this small community felt it hard.
scenes.headline: 2020 Border Closure

scenes.narration: Imagine living in your own country, and needing a passport to get home from the shops.
scenes.headline: Passport To Get Home

scenes.narration: A straight line drawn on paper in 1846 still decides how these people live today.
scenes.headline: A Line From 1846

scenes.narration: That was a line cutting through land. Next, a town that was left behind when a whole region changed hands.
scenes.headline: Next: A Left-Behind Town

scenes.narration: And that town sits beside a road that belongs to nobody.
scenes.headline: A Road Of No Country

scenes.narration: Number six: Llívia. It is a Spanish town sitting inside France, high in the Pyrenees mountains.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: Walk out of town in any direction and you step onto French land. The rest of Spain is a short distance away.
scenes.headline: France On Every Side

scenes.narration: It goes back to a treaty in 1659, when Spain handed France a number of villages in this area.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia counted as a town, not a village. So the treaty skipped it, and it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: One word in a treaty left a Spanish town stranded inside France, and nobody has changed it since.
scenes.headline: One Word Did This

scenes.narration: Today a road links Llívia to Spain. That strip of road is treated as neutral ground.
scenes.headline: Neutral Road

scenes.narration: Both countries are in the Schengen area, so you drive through with no border check, yet you still cross French land.
scenes.headline: No Check, Still Crossed

scenes.narration: The town has Spanish rules and Spanish street signs, with France on every side.
scenes.headline: Spain, Surrounded

scenes.narration: How can a single word in a treaty still matter after hundreds of years? Because borders stick.
scenes.headline: Borders Stick

scenes.narration: The next one is even stranger, because this time the village is German, but the country around it is Switzerland.
scenes.headline: German Inside Swiss

scenes.narration: And its shops run on Swiss money.
scenes.headline: Swiss Money

scenes.narration: Number five: Büsingen am Hochrhein. A German village that is separated from the rest of Germany by Swiss land.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: It sits on the Rhine river, with Swiss fields and Swiss towns all around it, yet it is legally German.
scenes.headline: German On The Rhine

scenes.narration: German law applies there, and people vote in German elections, but the village sits inside the Swiss customs area.
scenes.headline: German Law, Swiss Customs

scenes.narration: That means shops and businesses there widely use Swiss francs as well as euros.
scenes.headline: Francs And Euros

scenes.narration: A German village on Swiss money, inside a Swiss customs area, with German law. That is a tangled border.
scenes.headline: A Tangled Border

scenes.narration: Locals can walk into a Swiss town in minutes, and still be crossing a border on paper.
scenes.headline: Walk To Switzerland

scenes.narration: The border here is no great wall or fence. It is mostly a line on a map and small markers.
scenes.headline: Just A Marker

scenes.narration: Most days nothing looks different. That is exactly what makes it so strange.
scenes.headline: Nothing Looks Different

scenes.narration: You could pass through without noticing, and only a sign tells you which country's law applies.
scenes.headline: Only A Sign

scenes.narration: Now for number four, where the border and an airport share one road.
scenes.headline: Border Meets Airport

scenes.narration: And yes, that road used to cross the runway.
scenes.headline: A Road Over A Runway

scenes.narration: Number four: Gibraltar. A British territory at the southern tip of Spain, with a huge rock you can spot from far away.
scenes.headline: Gibraltar

scenes.narration: To enter from Spain, you walk or drive over the border, and then you meet a runway.
scenes.headline: Border, Then Runway

scenes.narration: For years, the main road to the border, Winston Churchill Avenue, crossed the airport runway at ground level.
scenes.headline: Road Across Runway

scenes.narration: When a plane was about to land or take off, barriers came down and the road simply closed.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: Cars, buses and people waited while an aeroplane passed right in front of them.
scenes.headline: Waiting For A Plane

scenes.narration: If you like strange places like this, subscribe, because there are more of them coming.
scenes.headline: More Strange Places

scenes.narration: In 2023, a tunnel opened for everyday traffic, so cars now go under the east end of the runway.
scenes.headline: The 2023 Tunnel

scenes.narration: Pedestrians and cyclists can still use the runway crossing, so the strange sight has not fully disappeared.
scenes.headline: Still Crossable

scenes.narration: The reason is simple: Gibraltar is tiny, and there was almost no flat land for an airport.
scenes.headline: No Flat Land

scenes.narration: Spain also claims Gibraltar, so this small border carries an argument that has run for a very long time.
scenes.headline: A Long Dispute

scenes.narration: Next, a piece of America that you reach through Canada, because of a mapmaker's mistake.
scenes.headline: A Mapmaker's Mistake

scenes.narration: Number three: the Northwest Angle in Minnesota. It is the only part of the lower 48 states north of the 49th parallel.
scenes.headline: Northwest Angle
scenes.visual_query: Northwest Angle Lake of the Woods

scenes.narration: It sits on Lake of the Woods, and by road you must drive through Canada to reach it.
scenes.headline: Through Canada By Road

scenes.narration: Like Point Roberts, it is American land that you reach through Canada.
scenes.headline: Like Point Roberts

scenes.narration: The story goes back to 1783, when a treaty described the border using a map that was wrong.
scenes.headline: The 1783 Treaty

scenes.narration: That map showed the Mississippi river beginning much farther north and west than it really does.
scenes.headline: Wrong River Source

scenes.narration: When the real source was found, the treaty line no longer made clean sense, and this corner was left over.
scenes.headline: A Leftover Corner

scenes.narration: In the end the corner stayed American, a small patch of land cut off by lakes and forest.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By Lakes

scenes.narration: Many visitors come by boat across the lake, or by plane.
scenes.headline: Boat Or Plane

scenes.narration: One wrong map from the 1700s still decides how you travel there today.
scenes.headline: A Map From The 1700s

scenes.narration: Now we move to India, with a border that is strange because of what happens there every evening.
scenes.headline: Now, India

scenes.narration: Two armies that rarely agree on anything perform together, and thousands of people come to watch.
scenes.headline: A Daily Show

scenes.narration: Number two: Wagah-Attari, the road crossing between Amritsar in India and Lahore in Pakistan.
scenes.headline: Wagah-Attari

scenes.narration: Every evening at sunset, crowds gather on both sides, and the soldiers put on a loud, high-kicking show.
scenes.headline: Sunset Ceremony

scenes.narration: Border guards from both countries march to the line with stiff steps, big boots and fierce looks.
scenes.headline: High-Kicking Guards

scenes.narration: It is called the Beating Retreat ceremony, and it has been performed for decades.
scenes.headline: Beating Retreat

scenes.narration: The crowds cheer, chant and wave flags, almost like a cricket match, but with soldiers.
scenes.headline: Like A Cricket Match

scenes.narration: Then the flags of both countries are lowered at the same time, and the gates are shut.
scenes.headline: Flags Down Together

scenes.narration: Two countries that have fought wars still perform a daily ceremony, side by side, with a gate between them.
scenes.headline: Rivals, Side By Side

scenes.narration: It is a rivalry and a performance in the same few metres, and everybody knows the steps.
scenes.headline: Rivalry As A Show

scenes.narration: Many Indians have sat in those stands and felt a strange mix of pride, noise and a border they could see.
scenes.headline: Pride And Noise

scenes.narration: But there is one Indian border with no show and no crowd, only a fence and a few metres.
scenes.headline: No Show, No Crowd

scenes.narration: Number one is high in the Himalayas, and it is the highest border on this list.
scenes.headline: Up In The Himalayas

scenes.narration: Number one: Nathu La, in Sikkim. It is a mountain pass at more than fourteen thousand feet.
scenes.headline: Nathu La

scenes.narration: On the other side is Tibet, which is part of China. The border runs right across the pass.
scenes.headline: Tibet On The Other Side

scenes.narration: Indian visitors with a permit can drive up from Gangtok and reach the border point. This visit is for Indian citizens.
scenes.headline: Permit Needed

scenes.narration: And when you get there, you stand metres away from Chinese soldiers, with a fence between you.
scenes.headline: Soldiers, A Fence Away

scenes.narration: Indian and Chinese guards stand on either side, close enough to see each other's faces.
scenes.headline: Face To Face

scenes.narration: This pass was once part of an old trade route between India and Tibet.
scenes.headline: An Old Trade Route

scenes.narration: After the 1962 war, it was shut. It reopened for trade in 2006, after decades.
scenes.headline: Shut In 1962

scenes.narration: Trade stopped again around 2020, and it has restarted after about six years.
scenes.headline: Trade Restarts

scenes.narration: So the same few metres hold soldiers, tourists and traders, in a place most of us only know from a map.
scenes.headline: Soldiers, Tourists, Traders

scenes.narration: That is what makes it the strangest: a military border that is also a trading post and a tourist stop.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest Border

scenes.narration: From a road through Canada to a fence in the clouds, every one of these borders is real.
scenes.headline: All Seven Are Real

scenes.narration: Your Nathu La visit puts you a few steps from Chinese soldiers. Next video: more places on the map that look fake but are real.
scenes.headline: Next: More Real Places
